claim: IAD Runway 01L/19R is 9,400 ft x 150 ft, with RWY 01L threshold elevation 296 ft and RWY 19R threshold elevation 277 ft.
supporting_excerpt: Runway 01L has dimensions of 9,400 ft x 150 ft with a threshold elevation of 296 feet, and runway 19R has dimensions of 9,400 ft x 150 ft with a threshold elevation of 277 feet.
caveat: 01C/19C is the 11,500 ft runway; the argument concerns 01L/19R. Confirm against current FAA airport master record / 5010.

claim: Under 14 CFR 77.19, a precision-instrument runway's approach surface rises at 50:1 for the first 10,000 ft then 40:1 for 40,000 ft, with a 1,000 ft primary surface widening to a 16,000 ft outer approach width.
supporting_excerpt: The approach surface extends for a horizontal distance of 10,000 feet at a slope of 50 to 1 with an additional 40,000 feet at a slope of 40 to 1 for all precision instrument runways; inner edge expands uniformly to a width of 16,000 feet; precision primary surface width is 1,000 feet.
caveat: Applies only if the relevant runway end is precision-instrument; confirm approach category per end.

claim: Under the Part 77 50:1 approach surface, a 50 ft object reaches the surface at only ~2,500 ft from the surface origin (200 ft beyond the runway end); a 70 ft object at ~3,500 ft.
supporting_excerpt: max_height_ft = distance_from_origin_ft / 50; 50 ft => 2,500 ft; 70 ft => 3,500 ft.
caveat: Flat-terrain assumption at runway-end elevation; true clearance depends on ground elevation and tallest-appurtenance height (operator site plan).

claim: FAA departure/takeoff clearance surface is 40:1, allowing only 25 ft of object height at 1,000 ft off the departure end.
source_title: FAA AC 150/5300-13B Airport Design (departure surface); TERPS 40:1 OCS
supporting_excerpt: 40:1 departure surface => max_height_ft = distance_ft / 40; 1,000 ft => 25 ft.
caveat: Cite exact table in current AC 150/5300-13B; confirm departure surface origin and departure-end geometry for 19R.

claim: FAA AC 150/5200-33 recommends 10,000 ft separation between a hazardous wildlife attractant and the AOA for airports serving turbine aircraft, and 5 statute miles where the attractant could cause hazardous wildlife movement into or across the approach or departure airspace.
source_title: AC 150/5200-33B, Hazardous Wildlife Attractants On or Near Airports
supporting_excerpt: For airports serving turbine-powered aircraft the recommended separation is 10,000 feet, and 5 statute miles if the attractant causes hazardous wildlife movement into or across the approach or departure airspace.
caveat: Confirm current revision (33C). A proposed stormwater retention pond is a recognized wildlife attractant class.

claim: A stormwater retention pond sited adjacent to the RWY 01L/19R end falls roughly 95% inside the 10,000 ft turbine-aircraft separation standard and ~98% inside the 5-statute-mile (26,400 ft) trigger distance.
source_title: Analyst construction from AC 150/5200-33 separation distances
supporting_excerpt: shortfall_ft = required_ft - actual_ft; at 500 ft actual vs 10,000 ft required, 95% inside; vs 26,400 ft, ~98% inside.
caveat: Actual separation is a placeholder pending the surveyed distance from the site plan; even a generous 2,000 ft leaves the pond 80% inside the standard.

claim: The only published numeric aviation threshold for a vertical exhaust/thermal plume treated as a hazard is CASA's 4.3 m/s vertical velocity; the FAA has no codified numeric equivalent.
source_title: CASA Advisory Circular 139.E-02, Plume rise assessments
supporting_excerpt: CASA guidance defines potential hazard to aviation posed by vertical exhaust plumes in excess of 4.3 metres per second (m/s) velocity.
airport_or_entity: CASA (Australia); referenced as anchor for US context
caveat: Australian standard; not a US regulatory threshold. Used as a reference anchor. A site-specific finding needs stack parameters run through a plume-rise model.

claim: On a standard 3-degree approach (50 ft TCH), aircraft overfly ~102 ft AGL at 1,000 ft from the threshold, ~155 ft at 2,000 ft, and ~207 ft at 3,000 ft - the control-critical band a plume or glare source would intersect.
source_title: Analyst construction from standard 3-degree glidepath geometry
supporting_excerpt: height_AGL_ft = 50 + distance_ft * tan(3deg); 1,000 ft => 102 ft; 3,000 ft => 207 ft.
caveat: Assumes straight-in 3.0-degree glidepath and 50 ft TCH; a flatter 2.75-degree path lowers overflight height ~8%.

claim: An ALSF-2 approach lighting system extends 2,400 ft from the runway threshold (3,000 ft where glideslope < 2.75 degrees), with lights at 100 ft spacing.
source_title: FAA ALSF-2 (High Intensity Approach Lighting System with Sequenced Flashing Lights)
supporting_excerpt: A full ALSF-2 approach lighting system is usually 2,400 feet, extended to 3,000 feet for an ILS glideslope less than 2.75 degrees; lights spaced at 100 ft intervals from the threshold outward.
caveat: Confirm the specific approach lighting system installed at the RWY 19R end.

claim: Hyperscale data-center campuses draw 100-500 MW (next generation 500-1,000+ MW), with 2.25-4 MW backup generator units in parallel fueled by on-site diesel or piped natural gas.
source_title: How Much Power Does a Hyperscale Data Center Use? (industry synthesis)
supporting_excerpt: Hyperscale AI campuses operate 100MW to 500MW; next-generation facilities plan 500MW to 1GW+. High-capacity generators range 2.25 MW to 4 MW, usually powered by on-site diesel or piped-in natural gas.
caveat: General industry ranges; the specific proposed facility's load and generation are operator data. Supports the 'energy-intensive, on-site generation' claim as typical, not certain.

claim: Two 2026 federal grants to Dulles total ~$64M ($41.8M Concourse E; $22.1M AIG FY2026), a documented floor for the prior federal investment Grant Assurance 29(C) protects.
source_title: Dulles Airport lands $41M federal grant for Concourse E construction; FAA AIG FY2026 award
supporting_excerpt: FAA awarded $41.8 million for Concourse E; MWAA received $22,121,621 for a new concourse under the FY2026 Airport Infrastructure Grant program.
caveat: Documented recent floor only; cumulative decades of AIP/PFC/BIL airfield/NAVAID investment is far higher and requires FAA grant history to state precisely.
